messages:
alex: Hey team, onboarding a large customer (healthcare) for a POC. They require a PrivateLink/Interface Endpoint to our hosted control plane and want cross-account setup. Need a checklist and any gotchas for subnets, routing, and who accepts the endpoint on our side. Also they asked about how API keys are delivered over PrivateLink vs public.

mira: Thanks @alex. I'll own customer comms. Need a short presales checklist we can hand to their infra. Timeline: they want POC in 2 weeks.

sam: Quick checklist from SE side: 1) We'll publish a VPC Endpoint Service in our account (aws service name like com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-xxxx). 2) Customer creates Interface Endpoint(s) in their VPC and shares the endpoint ID for acceptance. 3) We accept the endpoint (can be manual or auto-accept via service settings). 4) Security group inbound rules: allow 443 from customer's endpoint ENIs (we recommend restricting to the endpoint security group). 5) DNS: use the private DNS name that the endpoint provides or publish a Route53 private hosted zone if they want a friendly name. 6) Test with curl against the endpoint ENI IP / DNS. 7) Optional: attach endpoint policy to limit which principals/paths they can call.

irina: Network notes / gotchas: - PrivateLink = no route table changes between accounts, so you don't need VPC peering.
- Subnets: customer must create interface endpoints in at least 2 AZs for HA, endpoints consume /28 IPs per AZ.
- NACLs: ensure ephemeral ports allowed 1024-65535 for return traffic.
- Security groups: the endpoint ENIs get IPs in the target subnet; lock inbound to 443 from the endpoint SG (or specific CIDRs if they insist).
- DNS: if they enable "private DNS name" the standard public hostnames resolve to the endpoint inside their VPC; otherwise give them the endpoint-specific DNS names.
- If they use strict egress rules, endpoint needs outbound internet (no, PrivateLink is internal) — but kernel-bounced services still need NAT for other dependencies.

jack: For API key delivery: we do not transmit keys over the endpoint automatically. Options: 1) We upload a short-lived provisioning API key (rotate on acceptance) and provide it via the control plane once their endpoint is accepted; that traffic will flow over PrivateLink if they call our control plane via the endpoint DNS. 2) Or they can register their own client cert and we enable mTLS on the endpoint (extra engineering). Recommend: create a scoped POC key with 24h expiry and share via secure channel (1Password / secure upload).

sam: Minimal endpoint policy example (they asked for policy to lock to specific actions):
```{
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "vpce:Connect",
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:SourceVpce": "vpce-0abc123def"}}
    }
  ]
}
```
Replace vpce-0abc123def with their endpoint ID.

irina: Extra operational notes: - If their subnets are private with no NAT, the endpoint ENIs still work but any health checks out to other public services will fail. - Make sure their AZs overlap with ours (we publish AZs in the service description). - If customer insists on cross-account VPC peering instead, we lose the private DNS convenience and will need explicit route table entries + security group updates; also additional blast radius.

ops-bot: Ticket #POC-5923 created for acceptance workflow and entitlements. Assignee: jack. ETA: 3 business days.

mira: One more ask from security: they want an audit trail for endpoint acceptance and key deliveries. Can we capture that?

jack: Yes — acceptance events are in CloudTrail (vpce-connection-accept). We also log key issuance in our internal audit service (audit-id attached to the POC key). I'll add that to the handoff doc.

sam: Testing steps we give the customer: 1) Create endpoints in two AZs, share endpoint IDs. 2) Run: `curl -k https://vpce-<id>.execute-api.<region>.vpce.amazonaws.com/health` or the private DNS we give. 3) Verify 200 and TLS cert name matches our control-plane CN. 4) If 403, check endpoint policy and SG.

alex: Perfect. Can someone paste the minimal TF snippet the customer can run to create an interface endpoint and SG? I can attach to the SOW.

irina: Minimal Terraform snippet (customer side):
```resource "aws_security_group" "vpce_sg" {
  name = "redwood-vpce-sg"
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
  ingress { from_port = 443; to_port = 443; protocol = "tcp"; cidr_blocks = [var.restrict_cidr] }
  egress { from_port = 0; to_port = 0; protocol = "-1"; cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"] }
}

resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "redwood_interface" {
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
  service_name = "com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-REPLACE_WITH_SERVICE"
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids = var.subnet_ids
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.vpce_sg.id]
}
```
Replace service name with the one we publish.

mira: Great — I'll assemble a one-page handoff with these steps, the Terraform snippet, and the timeline. Jack, can you update the ticket with the audit key policy and set it to auto-accept for this customer?

jack: Will do. Setting service to auto-accept for this specific account and adding audit metadata. I'll post once done. :+1:

alex: Thanks everyone — attaching this to the POC SOW. I'll ping if they hit a routing/403 during tests.
